claims.text: Chemical short-range ordering in HfNbTaTiZr forms specific HfTi and TiZr binary clusters.
The binary clusters develop into a percolative network of ordered B2-like structures.
B2-like ordering reduces the local lattice-distortion amplitude in HfNbTaTiZr.
Reduced lattice distortion suppresses high-frequency phonon scattering.
Percolative SRO increases lattice thermal conductivity relative to the random solid solution, provided the ordered clusters form continuous rather than isolated pathways.
The initial material is an equiatomic random solid solution of HfNbTaTiZr.
Random HfNbTaTiZr has severe lattice distortion and strong high-frequency phonon scattering because of random atomic-mass and size mismatches.
Monte Carlo or molecular-dynamics/Monte Carlo equilibration can be used to produce an SRO state in a refractory high-entropy alloy.
Controlled annealing or Monte Carlo equilibration of HfNbTaTiZr promotes HfTi and TiZr clusters and a percolating B2-like network.
Annealing at 800–1200 K enables SRO-forming diffusion while remaining below melting, and controlled cooling preserves SRO without macroscopic phase separation.
Ordering reduces the variance of local atomic environments while maintaining a continuous crystallographic pathway for phonon transport.
Ordered atomic arrangements minimize strain energy associated with random atomic-size mismatches.
A percolating network of SRO clusters creates low-resistance phonon-transport pathways that can outweigh scattering at SRO boundaries.
The SRO-ordered state will exhibit higher lattice thermal conductivity, narrower high-frequency phonon-mode FWHM, and lower RMS atomic displacement amplitudes than the random state.
Random HfNbTaTiZr has low thermal conductivity because random lattice distortions and mass variance produce strong phonon scattering.
Below the cluster-percolation threshold, or after growth into large incoherent precipitates, interface scattering causes a conductivity-decrease regime.
At sufficiently high temperature, dominant Umklapp scattering diminishes the conductivity benefit of reduced static distortion.
In MoNbTaW, SRO produced at 800 K affects dislocation mobility and provides additional screw-dislocation strengthening at 300 K, with the effect becoming negligible by 2000 K.
